one_line_description.value: Telegram provides developer APIs including an HTTP Bot API for bots and the Telegram API/TDLib for building customized Telegram clients.
one_line_description.quote: The Bot API allows you to easily create programs that use Telegram messages for an interface. The Telegram API and TDLib allow you to build your own customized Telegram clients.

has_public_api.quote: The Bot API is an HTTP-based interface created for developers keen on building bots for Telegram.

api_type.quote: You communicate with this server via a simple HTTPS interface that offers a simplified version of the Telegram API.

api_breadth.value: Broad: Bot API for messaging and bot workflows, plus TDLib for full custom Telegram client features; exact endpoint count is not stated in the fetched sources.
api_breadth.quote: TDLib supports all Telegram features and makes developing Telegram apps a breeze on any platform.

auth_methods.quote: Each bot is given a unique authentication token when it is created.

access_model.quote: We welcome all developers to use our API and source code to create Telegram-like messaging applications on our platform free of charge.

access_notes.value: Free self-serve registration: sign up for Telegram, log in at my.telegram.org, and fill out the API development tools form to get api_id/api_hash; bot tokens come from bot creation. Third-party client apps must comply with the API Terms of Service; no paid plan or sales contact is documented.
access_notes.quote: Sign up for Telegram using an official application. - Log in to your Telegram core: https://my.telegram.org. - Go to "API development tools" and fill out the form.

webhooks.quote: There are two mutually exclusive ways of receiving updates for your bot - the getUpdates method on one hand and webhooks on the other.

sdk_languages.quote: See description of our JSON, C++, Java and .NET interfaces.

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: Bot API changes are tracked in a public changelog; no formal deprecation or sunset policy is stated in the fetched sources.
api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: Recent updates are listed in the Bot API changelog.

verdict_reason: Telegram offers a free, self-serve Bot API, with bot tokens obtained when a bot is created. The Bot API is a public HTTP interface with broad messaging, webhook, payment, and Mini App capabilities. No sales contact or app review gate is documented for the Bot API; the missing official MCP server does not block core API integration.
open_questions: No official Telegram-operated MCP server was found in the vendor documentation or MCP searches; only third-party/community MCP pages appeared.

Community MCP server URLs surfaced in search results (including GitHub mcp-telegram, usecarly, sociahive, breakreach, apis.io, and Composio content) were not fetched into SOURCES, so they are not verified here.
No numeric API rate limits were found in the fetched documentation.
No dedicated sandbox/test environment is documented in the fetched pages; testing notes cover a sample API id and free Gateway API testing.
OAuth/OIDC and MTProto api_id/api_hash authentication are documented on separate pages; the cited auth_methods evidence covers the Bot API bot token.
Exact Bot API method/type count was not available in the fetched sources, so API breadth is described qualitatively.
OAuth scopes/permissions documentation was not found in the fetched pages.
